title: Using __slots__ to reduce object memory

spans.text: `__slots__` declares allowed attributes and can avoid a per-instance `__dict__`. It may reduce memory for many small objects, but measure on the target Python version rather than assuming a benefit. Unlisted attributes cannot be added, and dynamic attributes or some multiple-inheritance layouts are affected. For data classes, Python 3.10+ also provides `@dataclass(slots=True)`.
`value` is a declared slot stored on the object; the output is `7`.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Measure a representative workload with `tracemalloc` or `sys.getsizeof`; `__slots__` does not automatically speed up an entire application.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: `__slots__` is not a security boundary and does not make objects immutable. Plan `__weakref__` and inheritance behavior explicitly.
